prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: one game ability VFX token atlas, 1024x1024 square RGBA with a truly transparent background. Exactly FOUR isolated hand-painted fantasy effect emblems in an exact evenly spaced 2 by 2 cell grid. Cell centers at 25% and 75% of image width/height. Keep each emblem entirely within the central 65% of its cell, with transparent gutters and no crossing between cells. No text, labels, frames, circles around icons, UI buttons, background, full characters, numbers, decorative borders, shadows or scenery. These are small rendered effect tokens and HUD icons; actual range shapes are rendered separately by the game. Strong distinct silhouette, detailed painted material, restrained glow, readable at 32px. Avoid large opaque panels. Depict characteristic tools/energy/material symbols, not a screenshot or miniature scene. Cell order: TOP LEFT passive, TOP RIGHT skill1, BOTTOM LEFT skill2, BOTTOM RIGHT ultimate. Original avatar: Bram Stonebranch. Character visual motifs: hulking aging simian monarch with a living leaf crown, wide moss-gold shoulder armor and a **short broad jade scepter**; no staff clone army or circle of striking monkey echoes.
TOP LEFT: Old Growth. Ability concept: when Bram blocks a *lobbed* projectile with canopy cover, he gains one Sap (max 2), empowering his next small shield. Direct low shots are unaffected by canopy.
TOP RIGHT: Root Column. Ability concept: plants a 2-HP vertical trunk column for 5 s at a legal position, 45-GU radius. Walkers pass around; two columns can support a canopy.
BOTTOM LEFT: Leaf Intercept. Ability concept: grows a **short overhead roof** between two active columns for 3 s. The roof can absorb up to two **lobbed** enemy projectiles; arching artillery is intercepted, low trajectories pass under. If only one column exists, Bram grants that column a small self-shield instead.
BOTTOM RIGHT: Kingdom of Shade. Ability concept: raises three additional short-lived columns forming a 130-GU **open canopy grove** for 5 s. Within it allies take reduced area-splash damage from above, but enemies can walk in, attack the exposed columns, or aim direct projectiles underneath. Canopy doesn't cancel ground hazards.
